subject: ophthalmology
title: Diseases of the macula

steps.tx: **Dry age related macular degeneration** (elderly, smoking, family, pale fundi) seeds **drusen** (discrete, soft confluent) with pigment clumping, distorting lines on Amsler grid while sparing periphery; large soft drusen with pigment change mark intermediate disease. **AREDS2** antioxidants with zinc slow intermediate progression in selected patients while smoking cessation and Mediterranean patterns protect. Geographic atrophy ( sharply demarcated chorioretinal loss) advances centrally despite supplements, needing low vision aids with emerging complement inhibition debates.
steps.say: Drusen plus pigment change in elderly with bent lines: dry AMD. AREDS2 slows intermediate disease.

steps.tx: **Wet (neovascular) AMD** bleeds or leaks beneath macula (subretinal blood, fluid, pigment epithelial detachment) crashing central vision; OCT with fluorescein or OCT angiography confirms choroidal new vessels. **Anti VEGF** injections (ranibizumab, aflibercept patterns: loading then treat and extend) dry and stabilise most, with endophthalmitis and systemic cautions counselled; photodynamic therapy suits polypoidal variants. Delay scars disciform permanently. Fellow eye Amsler self monitoring catches conversion early.
steps.say: Sudden bent lines with blood under macula: wet AMD, inject anti VEGF now. Delay scars forever.

steps.tx: Interface disorders: **macular hole** (full thickness foveal defect with Watzke Allen slit sign, vitreous traction in elderly) needs vitrectomy with internal limiting membrane peel and face down gas posturing for closure; lamellar holes observe mostly. **Epiretinal membrane (macular pucker)** wrinkles with cellophane reflex and metamorphosia, peeling when reading fails. Vitreomacular traction with oedema releases by vitrectomy or ocriplasmin debates. Pseudoholes mimic with intact outer layers on OCT.
steps.say: Slit of light broken at centre: macular hole, peel and posture. Wrinkled cellophane with bent vision: pucker.

steps.tx: Other maculopathies: **central serous** (young stressed men, steroids, smokestack leak) mostly settles with trigger removal; **myopic maculopathy** (lacquer cracks, Fuchs spot, choroidal new vessels in long eyes) needs anti VEGF for membranes with lifelong surveillance; **Stargardt disease** (juvenile beaten bronze macula with flecks, ABCA4 recessive) counsels against vitamin A excess and sun while gene trials run; **Best vitelliform** (egg yolk lesion, EOG abnormal) observes mostly. Solar and welder maculopathy burn photoreceptors with history.
steps.say: Young stressed steroids plus blurred spot: central serous, stop trigger. Beaten bronze flecks in teen: Stargardt.
